![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/2bf88537e9a37404dd10dd99769f6933879d07c1ffbb913adc2a4f52b11f48d6.png)

Consider the finite region above bounded by $y=\sqrt{x}$ and $y={x}^{3},$ as shown above. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $g(x)={x}^{3}.$

First, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ \sqrt{x} & ={x}^{3} \\ \sqrt{x}-{x}^{3} & =0 \\ \sqrt{x}(1-{x}^{5/2}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the limits of integration are from $x=0$ and $x=1.$ 

Let's draw our vertical arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing *away* from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/0cdcf559f1498045d3d8cd725593da6adb0459addb1df7cc3c4167b2fd9b6214.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $y=g(x)={x}^{3},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $y=f(x)=\sqrt{x}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({[\sqrt{x}]}^{2}-{[{x}^{3}]}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}(x-{x}^{6})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{7}}{7})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\pi [(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{7})-0] \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{14}.\end{aligned}
$$
